long_biography.plain_text:
Pruuli studied journalism in Tartu and began as a reporter before Estonia restored its independence. He then served Lennart Meri at the foreign ministry and advised prime minister Mart Laar. This work placed him close to the institutions of the new state before he moved into private enterprise.

Business brought him into the ownership group that assembled Go Group around travel, buses and rail. He later increased his stake while leaving daily decisions to professional executives. That structure preserved space for books and expeditions: after an early circumnavigation, he helped organise journeys to Antarctica and the Arctic and led a successful Northwest Passage expedition.

proposed_details.existing_value:
As reported by the Estonian newspaper ERR and the television show "Bellingshauseniga Arktikas," Tiit Pruuli, an Estonian journalist, is the proud owner of the vessel known as Admiral Bellingshausen. The boat was christened in honor of Fabian Gottlieb von Bellingshausen, a celebrated explorer and a distinguished officer in the Imperial Russian navy.

In a historic achievement during October 2023, Admiral Bellingshausen etched its name in the annals of Estonian maritime history by becoming the first sailing vessel from Estonia to successfully navigate the Northwest Passage. The journey took the vessel to Kotzebue in Alaska and enabled explorations of remote Arctic regions.
